01.actor: Rav Hisda, and a man who betrothed a woman with a blue stone
01.event: A man betrothed a woman with a blue marble stone, and Rav Hisda appraised it and ruled on her status, rejecting a mother's objection.
01.turn: The stone was no longer worth a peruta, and the man's mother objected that it had been worth that much on the day of betrothal.
01.outcome: Rav Hisda answered that she cannot make the woman forbidden to a later man, and compared it to Yehudit and Rabbi Hiyya's mother-in-law-style claim.
01.summary: A man betrothed a woman with a blue stone and Rav Hisda sat appraising it, ruling that if it was not worth a peruta she was not betrothed. The man's mother protested that it had been worth a peruta on the day of betrothal. Rav Hisda replied that she could not make the woman forbidden to a later suitor, and likened this to Yehudit, who tried to leave Rabbi Hiyya over a claim from her mother about her betrothal and was told her mother had no power to forbid her to him.
01.missing: The stone episode is mostly a legal ruling with a brief exchange, and the ending of the Yehudit comparison is only sketched.

03.actor: Rav Hiyya bar Adda, schoolteacher of Reish Lakish
03.event: Rav Hiyya bar Adda was absent for three days and, asked why, said he had been harvesting from the one vine his father left him.
03.turn: Each day's harvest of 300 clusters yielded less wine per cluster, and he gave away over half.
03.outcome: Reish Lakish told him the yield would have been greater had he not interrupted the children's Torah study.
03.summary: Rav Hiyya bar Adda, who taught Reish Lakish as a child, missed three days of teaching. When Reish Lakish asked why, he explained he had been harvesting one vine his father left him, 300 clusters a day, with each cluster filling a jug on day one, one jug per two clusters on day two, and per three on day three, and he gave away more than half. Reish Lakish replied that had he not been absent, the vine would have yielded even more.

04.event: Asked about the rival wife of a daughter, Rabbi Yehoshua declined to rule between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel.
04.turn: He said he feared the two great schools would break his skull, but offered testimony instead.
04.outcome: He testified that two great Jerusalem families descended from rival wives, including High Priests, showing the practice.
04.summary: People asked Rabbi Yehoshua about the rival wife of a daughter, and he said it was a dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel. Pressed on whose view is law, he asked why they were putting his head between two great mountains, fearing they would crush his skull. Instead he testified that two great Jerusalem families descended from rival wives who remarried, and High Priests came from them.

05.event: Ravina, who held his orphan nephew's wine, asked Rav Ashi whether he could take it along with his own wine to Sikhra.
05.turn: He was unsure whether to sell the orphan's wine at that time.
05.outcome: Rav Ashi told him to go, since the orphan's wine is no better than his own.
05.summary: Ravina held wine belonging to his orphaned nephew, Ravina the younger, and also had wine of his own that he was taking to Sikhra to sell. He asked Rav Ashi whether he might bring the orphan's wine along. Rav Ashi told him to go, since the orphan's wine was no better than his own.

06.actor: A blind man who reviewed mishnayot before Mar Shmuel
06.event: The blind man was late, Mar Shmuel sent a messenger, the messenger missed him and returned reporting that the blind man's wife had committed adultery.
06.turn: The blind man came to Mar Shmuel to ask whether he must heed this single report.
06.outcome: Mar Shmuel told him to divorce her if he trusted the messenger, and not to if he did not.
06.summary: A blind man who reviewed mishnayot before Mar Shmuel failed to show up one day, so Shmuel sent a messenger after him. They took different routes and missed each other, and the messenger went to the man's house and came back saying the man's wife had committed adultery. The blind man came to Shmuel, who told him: if you trust the messenger, divorce her; if not, do not.

07.actor: A man who deposited silk, and Rabbi Abba
07.event: A man deposited silk with Rav Dimi, who died without saying anything, and the claimant came before Rabbi Abba.
07.turn: No one knew whose the silk was after Rav Dimi died.
07.outcome: Rabbi Abba awarded it to the claimant because Rav Dimi was not wealthy and the claimant gave a distinguishing mark, provided he did not regularly come and go there.
07.summary: A man left silk in the house of Rav Dimi, brother of Rav Safra, who died without leaving instructions. The claimant came before Rabbi Abba, who ruled for him, since Rav Dimi was known not to be wealthy and the claimant described the silk, with the caveat that this holds only if he was not a regular visitor to the house.

08.event: A sharecropper betrothed a woman with a handful of onions taken from the field he worked and asked Rava about her status.
08.turn: Rava asked who had relinquished the onions to him, implying they were stolen.
08.outcome: Rava ruled the betrothal fails for a handful, though a whole bundle would be fine since the sharecropper could say one bundle for another.
08.summary: A sharecropper betrothed a woman with a handful of onions from the field where he worked and came before Rava. Rava asked who had given him permission to take them, treating them as stolen so the woman was not betrothed. He added that if it had been a bundle, the sharecropper could have said he took one bundle and the owner may take one, since they split the crop anyway.

09.actor: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi on his deathbed
09.event: As he was dying, Rabbi named Babylonian places and their people, including one village that turned away after trapping fish on Shabbat and was excommunicated.
09.turn: The Bireta DeSatya villagers desecrated Shabbat and became apostates after excommunication, while Adda bar Ahava is singled out.
09.outcome: He says that today Adda bar Ahava, just circumcised, sits in Abraham's lap and Rav Yehuda was born in Babylonia.
09.summary: On his deathbed Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi described several Babylonian towns, such as one full of Ammonites and one of mamzerim, and one whose people trapped fish on Shabbat, were excommunicated by Rabbi Ahai, and became apostates. He then mentioned Adda bar Ahava, who that day was circumcised and sits in Abraham's lap, and said Rav Yehuda was born that day in Babylonia.
09.missing: Mostly a list of statements rather than a sequence of events; only the fish-trapping episode is a small story.

10.event: Two deeds on the same property came before Rav Yosef, one dated the fifth of Nisan and one only 'Nisan'.
10.turn: The holder of the undated deed protested that he would lose.
10.outcome: Rav Yosef told him his deed could be from the twenty-ninth, so the property went to the specific date; when asked for authorization to repossess later sales, Rav Yosef noted the buyer could say his deed is from the first.
10.summary: Two deeds for the same property came before Rav Yosef, one dated the fifth of Nisan and one just 'Nisan'. He awarded the property to the holder of the fifth of Nisan deed. The other protested, and Rav Yosef answered that his deed might be from the twenty-ninth. The man then asked for a document allowing him to repossess property sold from Iyyar on, and Rav Yosef said a purchaser could reply that his deed is from the first of Nisan.

12.actor: A man who betrothed a woman with stolen dinars
12.event: A man grabbed coins from another person, threw them to a woman washing her feet and declared her betrothed.
12.turn: He then asked Rava whether she was betrothed.
12.outcome: Rava ruled that the owner has not despaired of the money, so the stolen dinars were not his and the betrothal has no effect.
12.summary: A woman was washing her feet in a basin when a man snatched dinars from someone else, threw them to her, and said she was betrothed to him. He later asked Rava about her status. Rava said the money was not truly the man's, since an owner is presumed not to have given up on stolen money, so the betrothal did nothing.

13.actor: Rabba bar bar Hana and Rabbi Yochanan
13.event: Rabba bar bar Hana recalls following Rabbi Yochanan to eat Genosar fruits, where Rabbi Yochanan would eat huge amounts.
13.turn: Rabbi Yochanan then said he had not tasted something that nourishes, which seems to contradict the earlier ruling that fruit is nourishment.
13.outcome: The Gemara corrects the wording to say he had not tasted sustaining food.
13.summary: Rabba bar bar Hana recalled going with Rabbi Yochanan to eat the fruits of Genosar, where each person took ten or a hundred fruits and Rabbi Yochanan ate them all. He would then swear he had not tasted nourishment. The Gemara, finding this difficult, says the wording should be that he had not tasted sustaining food.
13.missing: Habitual recollection told as a proof, not a single dated incident.

14.event: Another presumptive-priest case came before Rabbi Yochanan while Reish Lakish and Rabbi Elazar sat there, and Reish Lakish demanded evidence that the man received a share at the threshing floor.
14.turn: Rabbi Yochanan answered, 'And if there is no threshing floor, does priesthood cease?', the same line Rabbi Elazar had earlier said.
14.outcome: Reish Lakish glared at Rabbi Elazar and rebuked him for not citing the statement in Rabbi Yochanan's name.
14.summary: Earlier, Rabbi Elazar had answered Reish Lakish's insistence on a threshing-floor share with the remark that priesthood does not cease if there is no threshing floor. Later, with the three sitting before Rabbi Yochanan, a similar case arose, Reish Lakish repeated his demand, and Rabbi Yochanan gave the same retort. Reish Lakish then looked sharply at Rabbi Elazar and complained that he had heard the teaching of Rabbi Yochanan and not told them it was in his name.

15.actor: A couple who performed halitza in prison
15.event: A couple performed halitza privately in prison and the case came before Rabbi Akiva, who validated it.
15.turn: It is questioned how anyone could know what happened between them; witnesses saw from outside.
15.outcome: Rav Yehuda says the incident and the case both took place in prison, and witnesses watched from outside.
15.summary: A mishna tells of a couple who performed halitza alone in prison, a case that Rabbi Akiva validated. The Gemara asks how anyone knew what passed between them and answers that witnesses watched from outside. It then asks whether the act took place in prison or only came before Akiva there, concluding both were in prison.
15.missing: The incident itself is only referred to from the mishna, not told in the segments shown; the passage is mostly discussion of it.

16.event: Rav Aha bar Yaakov permitted the freed sons of Yudan the maidservant to marry each other's wives, and Rava objected that Rav Sheshet prohibited it.
16.turn: Rava challenged him with Rav Sheshet's opposite ruling.
16.outcome: Rav Aha replied that Rav Sheshet prohibited it and he permits it.
16.summary: The sons of Yudan the maidservant were freed, and Rav Aha bar Yaakov permitted them to marry each other's wives. Rava objected that Rav Sheshet had forbidden this, and Rav Aha answered that Sheshet forbade it but he permits it.
16.missing: A brief ruling and exchange, with no real development.

17.actor: A creditor and the herdsman of orphans
17.event: A creditor seized an ox from the herdsman of orphans, claiming he seized it during the debtor's life, while the herdsman said it was after death.
17.turn: The herdsman had no witnesses that the creditor seized it from him.
17.outcome: Rav Nachman ruled that since the creditor could simply claim he bought it, he is believed that he seized it during the debtor's life.
17.summary: A creditor seized an ox from the herdsman of orphans, saying he did so while the debtor was alive, which would make it valid; the herdsman said it was after the debtor's death. They came before Rav Nachman, who asked the herdsman for witnesses and heard he had none. He ruled the creditor was believed, since he could have said he bought the ox.

18.event: Ulla, who often went up to Eretz Yisrael, died outside it, and Rabbi Elazar was told.
18.turn: Rabbi Elazar quoted that he died in an unclean land, even though they said his coffin was coming to Eretz Yisrael.
18.outcome: Rabbi Elazar said that being absorbed by the land after death is not like being absorbed while alive.
18.summary: Ulla used to go up to Eretz Yisrael, but he died abroad. When told, Rabbi Elazar said Ulla had fulfilled the verse about dying in an unclean land. They answered that his coffin was being brought to Eretz Yisrael, and Rabbi Elazar replied that being taken in by the land after death is not the same as being taken in while alive.

19.actor: The wife of Rav Yosef, son of Rava
19.event: The wife of Rav Yosef son of Rava came before Rav Nechemya and asked for sustenance and then wine.
19.turn: She asked for wine as well as sustenance.
19.outcome: Rav Nechemya granted both, saying the people of Mechoza are known to drink wine.
19.summary: The wife of Rav Yosef, son of Rava, came before Rav Nechemya and asked him to fix her sustenance, which he did. She then asked for wine, and he granted that too, explaining that the people of Mechoza are known to drink wine.

20.actor: Mar Yehuda, Rav Yosef and Rav Shmuel, and Rabba
20.event: Mar Yehuda met Rav Yosef and Rav Shmuel at Rabba's door and drew an inference from a baraita, then raised a contradiction from another.
20.turn: They had no answer, and went to Rabba, who said a quarrelsome person had put them up to it.
20.outcome: Rabba resolved it by saying the first baraita concerns an animal slaughtered and found a tereifa.
20.summary: Mar Yehuda found Rav Yosef and Rav Shmuel at the door of Rabba's study hall and told them a baraita from which he inferred Rabbi Shimon holds the prohibition is not by Torah law. He then raised a contradiction from another baraita, and they were silent. They took the difficulty to Rabba, who said a troublemaker had set them up and resolved it by saying the first baraita deals with an animal slaughtered and found to be a tereifa.
